sentence: SYSTEM MODEL AND PROBLEM STATEMENT A.
label: none

sentence: System Model Figure 2 illustrates a smart factory environment, which comprises a factory floor, an edge network, and a remote cloud.
label: none

sentence: The factory floor comprises human operators, dynamic objects such as ATRs, forklifts, and static obstacles like pallets.
label: none

sentence: ATRs are assisted by visual object detection in order to pick up the components without human assistance and deliver them to SUBMITTED TO IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON NETWORK SERVICE AND MANAGEMENT 5 the production line.
label: none

sentence: Multiple cameras, each equipped with an Image Analysis module, are mounted in the area.
label: none

sentence: Each camera transmits the captured video to the Image Analysis module via REST API, which is typically used in industrial systems for inter-component communication [37].
label: none

sentence: The captured video streams are analyzed in the Image Analysis module to detect, classify, identify, position, and track the objects on the factory floor to build a world model that can be used for objects’ traveling, scheduling, and obstruction avoidance.
label: none

sentence: For instance, scheduling ATRs’ travel paths involves planning how ATRs should travel to arrive at the destination at a certain time and is based on a set of objects with predicted trajectories.
label: none

sentence: Almost all of the processing, such as travel planning and scheduling, is carried out in the edge network rather than the devices on the factory floor.
label: none

sentence: As shown in Fig. 2, the data collector in the edge network has the crucial task of collecting the data in the form of IIoT time-series metric data.
label: none

sentence: The time- series metric data can be either one-dimensional, where a se- quence of measurements from the same features are collected, or multi-dimensional, where a sequence of measurements from multiple features or sensors are collected.
label: none

sentence: The smart factory system may generate multi-dimensional series metric data with intricate features such as ATRs status, which is stationary or moving, or the wheel velocity of ATRs.
label: none

sentence: The raw collected metric data is passed to the Preprocessing module to clean and normalize.
label: none

sentence: The preprocessed data undergoes offline training to develop a time-series prediction model.
label: none

sentence: Subsequently, the trained model is deployed in the Anomaly Detector system, which is responsible for detecting application-level anomalies.
label: none

sentence: Moreover, the data collector also receives an online metric data stream and feeds it to the Anomaly Detector in order to carry out a real-time detection of anomalies.
label: none

sentence: Ideally, detecting anomalies should be as simple as comput- ing the distance between the ground truth (i.e., class labels) and the target (i.e., record).
label: none

sentence: A record is a data sample at a specific moment within a series.
label: none

sentence: A record can take the form of a vector within a multi-dimensional time-series data or a scalar value within a one-dimensional time-series data.
label: none

sentence: However, data labels may not always be available in practice since labeling the data is often challenging, mainly because anomalous records (i.e., records that do not conform to normal or expected records), are rare compared to normal records.
label: none

sentence: To cope with this, a prediction-driven anomaly detection mechanism is needed, where the ground truth is replaced by their predicted values, which can be generated by a time-series prediction algorithm.
label: none

sentence: Clearly, such an approach is dependent on the accuracy of the prediction module, which is usually affected by the anomalous records in the historical data.
label: none

sentence: Due to the dynamic nature of configurations and workloads caused by, for instance, updates to ROS or replacement of ATRs, the distribution of incoming data may undergo frequent changes over time, resulting in concept drift.
label: none

sentence: This, in turn, leads to false anomaly detection and results in poor perfor- mance of the detection model.
label: none

sentence: Our proposed RealTimeOAW algorithm exploits two types of windows: (i) sliding window for the detection of the concept drift and (ii) adaptive window for storing newly arrived records.

sentence: The sliding window has a fixed size of Ls, which contains the most recent records.

sentence: If the number of records in the adaptive window exceeds La, the oldest records are removed from the window.

sentence: By keeping a window of recently arrived records, the adaptive window ensures that the algorithm can adapt to the changes in data distribution.

sentence: The sliding window Wi associated with data record ri contains Ls records from record i – Ls to record i.

sentence: The Anomaly Rate (AR) within the window can be calculated by considering both the anomaly probability and the number of anomalous data records in the corresponding window.

sentence: If the anomaly probability of each record data exceeds a pre-defined threshold T, i.e., AP(i) > T, then record i is considered as an anomalous record.

sentence: Let W denote the set of the anomaly probabilities in the given sliding window Wi as follows: W = {AP(i −Ls), . . . , AP(i −1), AP(i)} .

label: none

sentence: In contrast, model training hyperparameters balance training speed and model performance and include parameters such as batch size SUBMITTED TO IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON NETWORK SERVICE AND MANAGEMENT 11 and epoch number.

sentence: It is important to note that these hyperpa- rameters have a direct impact on the structure, effectiveness, and efficiency of the LSTM models.

sentence: Time Complexity In the following, we present the time complexity of our proposed method.
label: none

sentence: In our proposed method, matrix calculations can be used to formulate the calculation of SID, allowing the calculations to be performed in parallel.
label: none

sentence: As a result, the calculation of WSD and RD can be further accelerated.
label: none

sentence: By leveraging the Scalable Universal Matrix Multiplication Algorithm (SUMMA) [41], we can significantly reduce the time complexity of computing WSD in Eq. (9) from O(L3) to O(L).
label: none

sentence: Additionally, the computation of WSD and SID in Eq. (10) can be efficiently performed in parallel since both involve a vector-matrix multiplication.
label: none

sentence: This parallelization requires only L arithmetic operations, resulting in a time complexity of O(L2/L) = O(L).
label: none

sentence: Moreover, multiplying the matrices in Eq. (10) can be accomplished with a complexity of O(L).
label: none

sentence: It is important to note that the matrix RD contains L×L entries of record distance, and each entry is calculated using Eq. (7).
label: none

sentence: Therefore, updating RD (upon arrival of a new record) runs with the complexity of O(L2D/L2) = O(D), where D is the record dimension.
label: none

sentence: Consequently, by incorporating parallelization techniques, the time complexity of computing SID(i) is reduced to O(D + L).
label: none

sentence: As a result, by increasing the number of dimensions, the time complexity of calculating the SID metric grows linearly.
label: none

sentence: The PDAD-SID algorithm time calculates RD between each pair of records with a time complexity of O(D) without any parallelization.
label: none

sentence: Thus, the time complexity for obtaining WSD between two sequences is O(LD).
label: none

sentence: Therefore, the time complexity of detection at a single record is O(L2), because L sources of predictions are used (see Eq. (12)).
label: none

sentence: With proper parallelization, the time complexity can be reduced to O(D+L).
label: none

sentence: Moreover, the training complexity of RealTimeOAW is O(MH).
label: none

sentence: Here, M denotes the number of records, while H represents the maximum number of iterations for hyperparameter search using the GA.
label: none
